name: latexml
why: Converting LaTeX into structured XML and MathML is a fascinating transform, though it is document tooling at heart.

brief.what_it_is: LaTeXML is a converter that takes LaTeX (or TeX) source documents and turns them into LaTeXML's own XML format. From that XML it can produce HTML in several flavors with MathML and SVG, or other formats such as JATS and ePub. Its distinctive output is mathematics rendered as both content and presentation MathML. The homepage names the executables latexml, latexmlc, latexmlfind, latexmlmath and latexmlpost, but it does not explain what each one does.
brief.why_it_exists: It was started during development of the Digital Library of Mathematical Functions (DLMF), which needed LaTeX sources transformed into XML for further manipulation and for building the web site. The authors wanted a digital library to focus on the semantics of the material, and found no existing software suitable, so they built it in-house.
brief.how_it_works: LaTeXML emulates TeX as far as possible, implemented in Perl, and converts the TeX or LaTeX document into its XML format. That XML is modelled on typical LaTeX document structure and is inspired by HTML, MathML, OpenMath and others. The abstract document is then transformed further into the target output such as HTML, MathML, SVG, JATS or ePub.
brief.install_notes: The fetched pages say nothing about installation, runtimes, or configuration beyond the Perl-based design. The brew package lists five executables: latexml, latexmlc, latexmlfind, latexmlmath and latexmlpost. No commands were shown on the pages I read.
brief.standout: Rather than translating LaTeX markup directly, it emulates TeX's processing and produces a semantic XML intermediate, so the same document can feed HTML, MathML and other outputs. It emits both content and presentation MathML for math, and arXiv has offered experimental HTML preprints built with it.
brief.status: Unknown. The homepage announces 'Now available: LaTeXML 0.8.8!' but gives no release date, and I did not check a repository or commit history. The homepage and the DLMF-hosted copy of the manual both loaded with the same content.
brief.caveats: The homepage itself says 'emulating TeX is kinda hard' and that 'there are gaps in fidelity and coverage', so some LaTeX packages and documents will not convert faithfully. The brew caveats field is empty. I found no platform, licence or build notes on the pages I read.
quotes: The approach is to emulate TeX as far as possible (in Perl), converting the TeX or (LaTeX) document into LaTeXML's XML format.
Of course, emulating TeX is kinda hard, there are many clever LaTeX package developers, and the Web moves quickly, so there are gaps in fidelity and coverage.
At the time, we found no software suitable to our needs, so we began development of LaTeXML in-house.
